# Paperband

> Paperband is a pluggable static-site and PDF builder for structured Markdown content
> ("cards"), run as a Maven plugin. This file is a single, self-contained reference an LLM
> (or a new human) can read to understand what Paperband can do and how to drive it.

It condenses the full guide
(`guide/src/main/paperband/content/`) — consult that for prose depth; this file is the
operational reference.

## What Paperband is

Paperband (`dev.noregressions.paperband`, Apache-2.0) is a pluggable static-site and PDF
builder for structured content — guides, runbooks, migration playbooks. One Markdown source
produces both a printable PDF and a browsable static HTML site. It runs as a Maven plugin
(`paperband-maven-plugin`), so books build inside `mvn install` and CI like any other artifact.

Requirements: JDK 21+, Maven 3.8+. PDF rendering uses Playwright (headless Chromium,
~300 MB download on first use, cached under `~/.cache/ms-playwright/`; set
`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` or pre-cache for offline CI — a missing Chromium fails the build,
there is no fallback renderer).

## Core concepts

- **Card** — one content file, normally `.md` with YAML frontmatter. The unit of authoring,
  the unit of site navigation (`cards/<id>.html`), and a named-destination anchor in the PDF
  (`#card-<id>`). Cards can also be `.html` (head = frontmatter, body = content) or pure
  `.yaml` (requires a `cardSchema:` in the book root).
- **Block** — a section inside a card. Every H2 (and H3–H6, nested rank-based like Pandoc
  `--section-divs`) starts a `<section class="block <slug>">`. The heading text is slugified
  into a CSS class (`## Watch Out` → `watch-out`); explicit override via Pandoc attribute
  syntax `## Heading {.class #id}`. Text before the first heading is the `intro` block.
  Conventional block names: intro, `what-changed`, `how-to-fix`, `watch-out`, `check` — but
  any heading works; themes style block classes.
- **Book** — a directory tree whose topmost `paperband.yaml` is the book root. Sub-folder
  `paperband.yaml` files layer configuration (the cascade, below).
- **Axis** — a categorical dimension (e.g. `tier`, `subsystem`) declared in the root yaml.
  Cards join a value via a frontmatter field of the same name, or a folder-level
  `axis:` binding (frontmatter wins). Each axis value gets: a PDF divider page, a site
  landing page (`{axis}-{value}.html`), nav entries, and a `{axis}-{value}` CSS class on the card.
- **Section** — folder-based grouping for cards with no axis value: each top-level folder is
  a discovered section, or `sections:` declares titled groups of folders. One divider page,
  one landing page (`<id>.html`), one nav entry per section.
- **Theme** — a directory of CSS (with a `manifest.txt`) plus optional Pebble template
  overrides. Appearance lives in themes; content carries only structure (enforced by the
  content policy, below).
- **Target** — a free-form name for an output profile (`pdf-a4`, `web`, …) that content can
  branch on via `where:` predicates. A target does NOT set page size or renderer.

## Conventional layout (zero configuration)

```
src/main/paperband/          ← <home>: default root every goal assumes
  paperband.yaml             ← book config: title, theme, axes, css, vars, sections
  content/                   ← the cards (.md, .html, .yaml-with-schema), any folder depth
  layouts/                   ← Pebble templates, snippets, block templates
  styles/                    ← css referenced by the css: chain
```

A book laid out like this needs no `<configuration>` at all. Override pieces individually
with `<home>`, `<content>`, `<layouts>`; legacy `<input>` walks any directory the old way.
`target/` and `node_modules/` are never walked.

## Quick start

```xml
<plugin>
  <groupId>dev.noregressions.paperband</groupId>
  <artifactId>paperband-maven-plugin</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
  <executions>
    <execution>
      <goals><goal>build</goal></goals>
      <configuration>
        <output>${project.build.directory}/book.pdf</output>
      </configuration>
    </execution>
  </executions>
</plugin>
```

Every goal also runs standalone, no POM edit needed:

```bash
mvn paperband:build -Dpaperband.input=path/to/book -Dpaperband.output=out.pdf
mvn paperband:site  -Dpaperband.input=path/to/book -Dpaperband.outputDirectory=out-site
mvn paperband:structure -Dpaperband.input=book     # resolved sections/cards, no render
mvn paperband:scan -Dpaperband.input=some/card.md  # one card's parsed blocks + resolved config
mvn paperband:pages -Dpaperband.pdf=out.pdf        # per-card page-span table from a built PDF
mvn paperband:renderers                            # list renderers + availability
mvn paperband:themes                               # list themes
mvn paperband:blocks                               # list ```type fences + what renders each
```

## Cross-references between cards

`[text](card:<id>)` — one form, resolved per output: PDF `#card-<id>`, site
`cards/<id>.html` spelled relative to the page carrying it (`../cards/<id>.html` from a card
page). `card:<id>#<block-anchor>` sharpens the SITE link; print ignores the fragment and
lands on the card, because block anchors are heading slugs with no card prefix and collide
across cards in one document. Ordinary markdown, so previewers and link checkers see a link.

CHECKED against the book being built: an unknown id or an unknown block anchor FAILS the
build (MojoFailureException, like the page budget), naming the file, aggregating every
broken reference, and suggesting near misses. A card excluded by `select:`/an edition gets a
distinct message. A single-card build (`-Dpaperband.input=card.md`) resolves but does not
check — it has no book to check against. Block anchors come from the block's `{#id}` or its
slugged heading, the same rule the templates render.

## Authoring cards (Markdown)

### Frontmatter fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | path-in-book, slugified | Stable identifier → PDF anchor + site URL. Load-bearing once published. |
| `title` | string | first H1 | With `title:` set, no heading is consumed; without it the first `#` becomes the title and is not repeated. |
| `oneliner` | string | — | Summary line shown in card meta and listings. |
| `effort` | string | — | `XS`/`S`/`M`/`L`/`XL` badge. |
| `tags` | list | — | Free-form; reserved for filtering. |
| `max_pages` | int | — | Per-card page budget; build fails (exit 3) if exceeded. Wins over `<maxPagesPerCard>`. |
| `verify` | bool | `true` | `false` suppresses `check`-classed blocks at every nesting depth. |
| `index` | list/string | — | Back-of-book index terms for this card. |
| `<axisName>` | any | — | Joins the card to that axis value (e.g. `tier: 1`). |
| anything else | any | — | Preserved; templates read it via `card.frontmatter.get("key")`. No schema validation. |

### Fenced code blocks

- Attributes on the info line (```` ```text {.output} ````) or on a line immediately after
  the closing fence (`{.fs--1}` — must be followed by a blank line). `fs--1`/`fs--2` shrink
  code ~10%/20% for wide lines in print.
- **Editorial shorthands**: the fence language IS the block type —
  ```` ```command ```` (highlighted bash, "Command" label), ```` ```output ```` (plain,
  "Output" label), ```` ```console ```` (mixed `$`-prefixed session). Real languages pass
  through untouched. On screen (site pages, emitHtml in a browser) `command`/`console`/`bash`
  blocks get a Copy button (console copies only the `$`-prefixed lines, stripped); opt
  any block in with `{.copy}`, out with `{.no-copy}` or `vars.copyButtons: false`; never
  shown in print.
- **Mermaid diagrams**: ```` ```mermaid ```` holds Mermaid diagram text, rendered to
  inline SVG on the site AND in the PDF (the renderer waits for diagrams to finish before
  snapshotting/measuring, so page numbers stay exact). `vars.mermaidTheme` picks mermaid's
  colour theme (`default`/`dark`/`forest`/`neutral`/`base`). A non-parsing diagram fails
  the PDF build with mermaid's error. The library loads from the CDN only when a page
  contains a diagram — offline build machines need network for books that use it.
- **Custom block types**: put a Pebble fragment at `layouts/blocks/<type>.html` and
  ```` ```<type> ```` renders through it. Model: `content` (verbatim, escaped — `| raw` is
  a choice), `type`, `classes`, `id`, `vars`. Resolution: theme templates → book
  `layouts/blocks/` → bundled. A template named after a real language (`java.html`)
  captures every such fence book-wide. A broken template fails the build naming card,
  type, and file.

### Includes and templating (every card body is a Pebble template)

Card bodies are evaluated as Pebble in ONE pre-pass before Markdown parsing. Frontmatter,
fenced code blocks, and inline code spans are masked (protected from evaluation); anything
else that looks like `{{ }}`/`{% %}` must be valid Pebble or wrapped in `{% verbatim %}`.

- `{% fragment "ref" %}` — embed **verbatim content** from a file:
  - `"path/file.java:AnchorName"` — region between `ANCHOR: name` / `ANCHOR_END: name`
    comments (any comment style).
  - `"path/file"` — whole file. `"pom.xml:1:5"` — 1-indexed inclusive line range.
  - `as="code"|"markdown"|"html"|"text"` overrides the extension-inferred return type.
  - Paths resolve against the card's directory first, then the book root. Missing file or
    anchor = hard build failure with source location. Reads outside the book root require
    `<externalIncludeDirs>`/`<externalIncludeFiles>` (containment).
- `{% include "snippets/name" %}` — embed a **live Pebble template** from `layouts/`
  (`.html` appended when no extension); takes params via
  `with {"k": "v"}`. Snippets evaluate (masking does not extend into them); no cycle
  detection — recursion fails the build.
- `{% import "macros/lib" %}` — macro libraries, same resolution.
- Vars: `{{ vars.key }}` interpolation and `{% if vars.flag %}…{% endif %}` gating. A false
  conditional removes the region (headings included) before block-splitting. Undeclared
  `vars` keys read as null/false — never an error; only real Pebble syntax errors fail.
- Built-in vars (seeded first, so yaml can override them for reproducible builds):
  `build_date`, `build_date_long`, `build_year`, `build_month_year`, `build_iso`.

### HTML and YAML cards

- **HTML card**: `<title>`/first `<h1>` = title, each `<meta name="x" content="y">` = a
  frontmatter field (values typed as YAML would type them). Body goes through the same
  pipeline (headings → blocks, Pebble with `<pre>`/`<code>`/comments masked, content
  policy). Allowed only where authorship is declared: under `content/`, or via a POM
  include pattern that itself ends in `.html`.
- **YAML card**: a flat YAML doc transpiled to markdown via the book root's `cardSchema:`
  (`frontmatter:` list of copied fields; `sections:` ordered list of
  `{field, heading?, level?, class?, fence?}` — absent fields are skipped; `fence:` emits
  a fenced block, list-valued fields emit one fence each).

### Content policy (structure vs appearance)

`vars.contentPolicy: allow | clean | strict` (default `clean`). `clean` strips presentation
from content HTML — inline `style=`, `<style>`/`<script>`, head-metadata tags,
presentational tags/attributes, `on*` handlers — logging each removal; classes and ids
survive (the sanctioned styling route), and table-cell `align` from GFM `---:` survives.
`strict` fails the build on the same findings; `allow` passes verbatim. Fenced/inline code
is never touched. Style content by naming meaning: `> text {.warning}` + a CSS rule.

## Configuration

### The cascade (root → folder → card)

Book root = the topmost directory with a `paperband.yaml`, found by walking up from each card.
Per-key merge rules:

| Key | Rule |
|---|---|
| `vars` | Map merge, innermost wins per key |
| `axis` | Folder axis bindings; merged into `vars` too; card frontmatter beats folder binding |
| `css` | Concatenated root-first (inner CSS wins ties) |
| `layout` | Last non-null wins |
| `targets` | Last non-empty list replaces wholesale |

Root-only keys (do not cascade): `title`, `axes`, `theme`, `sections`, `cardSchema`,
`cover`, `back`, book-wide `sections.landing.template`, `publication`.
Folder-local, non-cascading keys: `order`, `include`, `sort`, `where`, `ignore`.

### Root `paperband.yaml` shape

```yaml
title: "My Book"
theme: editorial                 # one of the built-ins, or a <themeDir> theme
targets: [pdf-a4, web]           # free-form names for where: predicates
css: [styles/book.css]           # book CSS chain (theme CSS inlines after it)
axes:
  - name: tier                   # the frontmatter key cards use
    title: Tier
    values:
      - { id: 1, label: "Tier 1 - Critical", color: "#c0392b" }
sections:                        # declared top-level grouping (list form)
  - title: "Foundations"
    folders: [01-getting-started, 02-authoring]
  - { title: "Appendix", folders: [99-appendix], landing: false }
vars:
  subtitle: "..."                # promoted to book.subtitle (also: series, author)
  toc: true                      # printed table of contents (PDF only)
  index: auto                    # back-of-book index; auto = frontmatter + TF-IDF terms
  indexStop: [generic, terms]    # veto auto index picks
  watermark: "DRAFT"             # or a map: {text|image, color, opacity, angle, font_size,
                                 #   bold, scale, fit, behind, tile, pages, font}
  contentPolicy: clean
  mermaidTheme: dark             # ```mermaid colour theme: default | dark | forest | neutral | base
  page:
    size: 6x9                    # a4 (default) | a5 | letter | legal | 6x9 | packt | {width,height,unit}
    margins: { top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0 }   # zero = full-bleed
    measure: 58rem               # text measure; overrides theme --card-max-width; `none` = full width
```

Undeclared axis values still get landing pages (generated label + default palette colour).
Cards on no declared axis group by top-level folder ("sections").

### Folder `paperband.yaml` — shape and ordering

Exactly ONE of these applies per folder (precedence: `sections:` > `include:` > `order:`;
a losing key alongside a winner warns):

| Key | Meaning | Unlisted files |
|---|---|---|
| `sections:` | Titled groups of subfolders | Discovered, appended after |
| `include:` | Exclusive list, this order only. A listed entry that resolves to nothing FAILS the build (an `order:` entry only warns) | Excluded silently (by design) |
| `order:` | These first, rest appended | Appended alphabetically or per `sort:` |
| `sort:` | Order by frontmatter field(s) | Sorted, not dropped |

Plus: `title:` (section display label), `axis: {name: value}` (binds every card beneath),
`ignore:` (gitignore-style skip list, filters discovery AND declared lists),
`landing: {template: <preset-or-path>}` (this section's landing/divider template —
presets `default` | `minimal`, or a path relative to `layouts/`).

`order:` entries can be maps with target predicates:
`- { id: interactive-demos, where: "target == 'web'" }` — false skips the card/subtree.
Note: `target` is visible only in `where:` predicates; card bodies see only `vars`.
Target strings are not validated — a typo silently selects nothing.

## Rendering

### Themes

Built-ins (9): `editorial`, `editorial-gold`, `classical`, `fieldguide`, `dark`,
`blueprint`, `carded`, `herodevs`, `workshop` (for repeating-rhythm lab/workshop docs).
Custom theme = a directory with `manifest.txt` (one CSS path per line; `#` comments) and
optionally `templates/`; pass via `<themeDir>`. Same-named theme overrides a built-in.
`<theme>none</theme>` disables theming entirely (scaffold CSS remains).

CSS inlining order (weakest → strongest): structural scaffold → book `css:` chain →
theme manifest CSS → build `<stylesheets>`. So a theme beats book CSS, and
`<stylesheets>` beats the theme ("that theme, with my corrections").

Stable CSS hooks for themes: block classes (`section.block.watch-out`), axis classes
(`article.card.tier-1`), page classes (`target-{t}`, `size-{s}`, `has-sidebar`),
component classes (`.card-title`, `.oneliner`, `.card-grid`, `.site-nav`,
`.section-divider`, `.book-toc`, `.book-index`), and geometry custom properties stamped on
`<html>`: `--pw-content-height`, `--pw-page-margin-*`, `--pw-font-scale`,
`--card-max-width`. Full-bleed themes need `box-decoration-break: clone` on the card plus
insets computed against `var(--pw-page-margin-*)`.

Template loader chain: **theme `templates/` → book `layouts/` → bundled defaults** —
any bundled template overridable by filename: `book.html`, `card.html`, `site-index.html`,
`site-card.html`, partials `_card-body.html`, `_block-section.html`, `_section-divider.html`,
`_tier-divider.html`, `_book-cover.html`, `_book-back.html`, `_site-sidebar.html`,
`_book-toc.html`, `_book-index.html`, `_book-front` (renders between cover and first card).
Partials pair as thin wrapper + `-base` (override the wrapper, extend the base, replace one
Pebble block).

Template model: `card` (`id`, `title`, `frontmatter.*`, `axes.{name}.{id,label,color}`,
`blocks` nested `{heading, level, classAttr, html, children}`, `slots`), `book`
(`title, subtitle, series, author, vars.*, cover, back`), `vars` (fully cascaded),
`axis`/`value`, `section`. `vars`/`frontmatter` are lenient (missing key → null);
structural objects are strict (typo fails the build). Extra axis-value yaml keys beyond
`id`/`label`/`color` are NOT exposed — put theme-visible data in `vars` or frontmatter.

Slot API for fixed-skeleton card templates: `card.slots.take(name|[aliases])`,
`require(name)`, `rest()`, `has(name)`. Once a template touches `card.slots`, every
top-level block must be placed and every `require` satisfied or the build fails (exit 4)
listing offenders. Delete `rest()` to turn the template into a strict shape check.

### Renderer and page geometry

One renderer ships: `playwright` (headless Chromium). It treats `PageSpec.size`/`margins`
as sole geometry authority (theme `@page` rules are ignored) and emits named PDF
destinations for every anchor — the basis of page reporting/enforcement. Before
snapshotting (and before measuring, so page counts agree) it waits for network-idle,
`document.fonts.ready`, and every promise page scripts push into
`window.paperbandPending` — the contract that gets JS-rendered content (mermaid diagrams)
into the PDF finished; a rejected promise fails the render with the script's error.

Four things inset content from the paper edge: page margin (`vars.page.margins` /
`<margins>`), built-in horizontal safety padding `max(0mm, 8mm - margin)`, the theme's text
measure (`--card-max-width`, retune with `vars.page.measure`), and per-page card padding
from the theme. "Full-bleed still looks margined" is usually the measure.

### TOC and index (PDF only; `site` ignores both)

`vars: {toc: true, index: auto}`. Real page numbers via a two-pass render (placeholders →
read named destinations → re-render; pagination cannot shift). `index: auto` adds TF-IDF
extracted terms (deterministic; ≤5 per card; stemmed/stopword-filtered; code identifiers
boosted; terms in >⅓ of cards dropped); curate with `indexStop`. Review picks without
rendering: `mvn paperband:structure` shows each card's resolved `index:` line. Headings via
`vars.tocTitle`/`vars.indexTitle`. In a POM-declared book, `<toc/>` is positional between
`<section>` elements (at most one); index is `<index>auto</index>` under `<book>`.

### Watermarks

`vars.watermark` (string or map) or `-Dpaperband.watermark=...`. One declaration marks BOTH
outputs: the PDF via a PDFBox post-pass (preserves named destinations), the site via a
`position:fixed; pointer-events:none` CSS overlay injected into every page before
`</body>` (class `pb-watermark` — a theme can restyle or hide it). `build`, `site` and
`render` all take the parameters; `publish` picks them up per edition through `vars`.

Keys (param / default): `text` (`<watermark>`) or `image` (`<watermarkImage>`, book-root
relative, copied to the site's `assets/`) — exactly one, both is an error; `color`
(`#888888`), `opacity` (0.12), `angle` (-30°), `font_size` (96pt, min 8), `bold` (true),
`scale` (0.5, image only), `fit` (true), `behind` (false), `tile` (false, 3x4 grid),
`pages` (`all` | `first` | `except-cover`, PDF only), `font` (TrueType to embed, PDF only).
Unknown keys are an error.

`fit` makes `font_size` a ceiling: the stamp shrinks until its rotated bbox is inside the
page (floor 8pt), so a long phrase no longer runs off the paper. Newlines in `text` (real or
the two characters `\n`) stamp as separate lines. Default Helvetica is WinAnsi — CJK /
Cyrillic / Greek needs `font:`; without it the build WARNS, names the characters, and
renders unmarked rather than failing. A missing image or unloadable font warns the same way.

In a POM, `<watermark>` is a BLOCK mirroring the yaml map (`<text>`, `<color>`, `<opacity>`,
`<angle>`, `<fontSize>` — camelCase for yaml's `font_size` — `<bold>`, `<image>`, `<scale>`,
`<fit>`, `<behind>`, `<tile>`, `<pages>`, `<font>`); `<watermark>DRAFT</watermark>` is the
bare-string shorthand. Alongside it the flat `<watermarkText>`/`<watermarkColor>`/… family
carries the `-D` properties. Three channels compose in a fixed order: `vars.watermark`, then
the POM block, then the flat params. The block REPLACES a yaml declaration's subject; a
block with only knobs retunes a yaml-declared stamp. `site` ignores `<pages>`/`<font>` inside
the block, but does NOT declare the flat `<watermarkPages>`/`<watermarkFont>` — put those two
in the build execution. `<emitHtml>` carries the overlay as screen-only (its print path is the PDFBox
stamp), which is why `render` takes the parameters at all.

### Page enforcement

`<reportPages>` prints a per-anchor table (cover, dividers, cards; START/PAGES/LIMIT).
`<maxPagesPerCard>` sets a global ceiling; frontmatter `max_pages` wins per card. Violation
→ exit code 3 (vs 2 = bad input/unknown renderer, 4 = slot-contract failure). Counting
requires named destinations; without them checks are skipped WITH a warning, not failed.
`mvn paperband:pages -Dpaperband.pdf=out.pdf` (`-Dpaperband.byPages=true` sorts longest
first, `-Dpaperband.cardsOnly=true` hides furniture rows) reads the same table from any
built PDF.

## Maven plugin reference

Goal prefix `paperband`. Ten goals:

| Goal | Does | Default phase |
|---|---|---|
| `build` | PDF from a card, book directory, or POM-declared book | `process-resources` |
| `site` | Static HTML site (index, landing pages, per-card pages with prev/next) | `process-resources` |
| `publish` | Every edition in the book's `publication:` block | `process-resources` |
| `structure` | Resolved sections/cards/blocks dump, no render | `process-resources` |
| `pages` | Page-span report from a rendered PDF | `verify` |
| `scan` | One card's frontmatter, blocks, resolved cascade | direct |
| `render` | One HTML file → PDF, no card pipeline (e.g. re-render a hand-edited `emitHtml`); takes the watermark params | direct |
| `renderers` | List renderers + availability | direct |
| `themes` | List themes (`-Dpaperband.themeDir=` to include custom) | direct |
| `blocks` | List ```` ```type ```` fences the build can render, and what renders each | direct |

Key parameters (every one has a `-Dpaperband.<name>` property):

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | — | Card file or book directory (legacy spelling; wrapper detection). Mutually exclusive with `book`. |
| `home` / `content` / `layouts` | `src/main/paperband` / `${home}/content` / `${home}/layouts` | Book geography; each build logs the resolved values. |
| `book` | — | POM-declared book (below). |
| `output` | required (build) | Output PDF. `site` uses `outputDirectory` + `<clean>`. |
| `renderer` | `playwright` | |
| `target` | `pdf-a4` (`site`: `siteTarget`, default `web`) | Feeds `where:` predicates. |
| `pageSize` | `a4` | Seeds base geometry; yaml `vars.page` still wins. |
| `margins` | page size's own | CSS shorthand: `0`, `18mm`, `20 15 25 15`; units mm/cm/in/pt. |
| `theme` / `themeDir` / `stylesheets` | book's `theme:` / — / — | Build `theme` overrides yaml; `none` disables. |
| `emitHtml` | — | Also write the pre-render HTML — standalone (local images inlined as data: URIs) with a screen-only nav sidebar (opt out: `vars.sidebar: false`). |
| `reportPages` / `maxPagesPerCard` | `false` / `vars.maxPagesPerCard` | |
| `select` | — | Keep only cards matching `field=value` (book builds). |
| `watermark` / `watermarkImage` | `vars.watermark` | Plus `watermarkColor/Opacity/Angle/FontSize/Bold/Scale/Fit/Behind/Tile/Pages/Font`. `site` takes all but Pages/Font; `render` takes all. |
| `externalIncludeDirs` / `externalIncludeFiles` | — | Allow-list fragment reads outside the book root. |
| `skip` | `false` | |

### POM-declared books (`<book>`)

Declares structure in XML with glob-selected cards — for shapes no folder layout expresses
(e.g. one `TRACE.md` per service directory) and for generated content with no home for a
yaml. Anything inside `<book>` WINS over the yaml; geometry outside it (`<margins>`,
`<pageSize>`) only seeds the base.

```xml
<book>
  <root>${project.basedir}</root>          <!-- must BE the book root -->
  <title>Incident Runbook</title>
  <cover><template>layouts/cover.html</template><fullPage>true</fullPage></cover>
  <footer><template>layouts/footer.html</template></footer>   <!-- also <header>, <back> -->
  <vars><subtitle>...</subtitle></vars>     <!-- FLAT STRINGS ONLY; nested data → yaml -->
  <axes><axis><name>tier</name><title>Tier</title>
    <values><value><id>1</id><label>Critical</label><color>#c0392b</color></value></values>
  </axis></axes>
  <sections>
    <toc/>                                  <!-- positional printed TOC; at most one -->
    <section>
      <title>Scenarios</title>
      <includes><include>services/*/TRACE.md</include></includes>
      <excludes><exclude>services/legacy/**</exclude></excludes>
      <sort>tier,-id</sort>                 <!-- frontmatter fields, - = descending -->
      <where>target != 'web'</where>
      <landingTemplate>minimal</landingTemplate>
      <landingPage>true</landingPage>       <!-- false = no divider/landing page at all -->
    </section>
    <page><template>matrix</template></page> <!-- generated page: whole-book model
                                                 (cards, sections, axisGroupings, book, vars) -->
  </sections>
  <index>auto</index>
</book>
```

Glob semantics: `glob:` patterns against paths relative to `<root>`; `*` stops at `/`,
`**` crosses (zero or more segments). Only card files match (`.md` except `README.md` —
a README is claimed only by a pattern naming it; `.html` only when the pattern itself ends
`.html`; `.yaml` only with a `cardSchema:`). An `<include>` pattern that matches no card
files at all FAILS the build naming the section and pattern; a pattern emptied only by an
earlier section's claim or the section's own `<excludes>` is legal (empty-section warning).
First matching section claims a file; matches
are never duplicated. `<book>` with no sections/includes = declared config over a walked
tree. Repeated singular elements (`<title>`, `<author>`, …) fail the build. `<author>` vs
`<authors>` (list; `book.author` renders "A and B") — declaring both is an error.
Caveat: declared axes and declared sections compete for the divider slot — a card
regrouped by axis loses its section divider; check with `paperband:structure`.

### The `publish` goal and `publication:` block

Several editions cut from one source (full guide / mini / client edition), all declared in
the root yaml; the POM contributes only session settings (`<bookDirectory>` required,
`<editions>` subset, `<emitHtmlDirectory>`, `<set>` dotted-path overrides like
`defaults.theme=carded` or `editions.mini.vars.audience=manager` — unknown paths are errors).

```yaml
publication:
  defaults:                      # all keys optional
    theme: editorial
    size: A5
    output: "target/{id}.pdf"    # {id} expands to the edition id
    themeDir: mythemes
    vars: { audience: everyone }
    pages: { report: true, maxPerCard: 3 }
  editions:
    - id: full                   # required, unique
      title: "The Full Guide"
      classes: [print]           # extra classes stamped on <html> beside edition-{id}
      theme: classical           # scalar keys override defaults
      vars: { audience: expert } # merged over defaults.vars
      select:                    # empty = every card; list ∪ query
        cards: [intro, quickstart]
        fields: { tier: 1 }      # frontmatter equality clauses, AND-ed
        where: "card.frontmatter.effort != 'XL'"
```

Editions build in declaration order; one failure doesn't stop the rest; the goal fails at
the end naming failures.

## Extension points

- **PDF renderer** — implement `dev.noregressions.paperband.render.HtmlToPdfRenderer`
  (`name()` is the `<renderer>` selector; override `isAvailable()` for external binaries),
  register in `META-INF/services/…HtmlToPdfRenderer` (true ServiceLoader SPI).
- **Block renderer** (`block.BlockRenderer`) — a ```` ```type ```` fence whose HTML is
  computed by a jar rather than a template. Declares `name()`, `types()` (the fence tags it
  claims), `isAvailable()`/`unavailableReason()`, and `render(BlockRequest)`; register in
  `META-INF/services/…block.BlockRenderer` (true ServiceLoader SPI). Installed by adding
  the jar to the **plugin's** `<dependencies>`. Precedence: theme/book
  `blocks/<type>.html` > BlockRenderer > bundled `blocks/<type>.html` > plain code block.
  Settings arrive as `vars.<rendererName>` (so they cascade). Two renderers claiming one
  type fails the build. `mvn paperband:blocks` lists every type and what renders it.
  Bundled implementation: `block-plantuml` (```` ```plantuml ````/`puml`/`uml` → inline SVG
  at build time, no browser and no network;
  `vars.plantuml.{theme,styleFile,style,background,format,scale}`). Theming a PlantUML
  diagram is NOT a CSS job — it bakes colours into each shape and emits no classes, so
  nothing can select them; use `styleFile:` (a PlantUML `<style>`/`skinparam` file, path
  relative to the book home) or inline `style:`. They compose broadest-first:
  `theme` → `styleFile` → `style`.
- **Content provider** (`include.ContentProvider`) — new fragment sources selected by
  scheme prefix (`git:path@ref`); and **fragment processor** (`include.FragmentProcessor`)
  — new `as="type"` conversions. Both currently wired explicitly in
  `Includes.defaultProviders()/defaultProcessors()`, NOT ServiceLoader-discovered.
- **Themes** — pure directories, no code (see Themes above).
- **Templates / block templates** — per-book overrides via `layouts/`, no code.

## Debugging workflow / gotchas checklist

1. Wrong blocks or classes on a card → `mvn paperband:scan -Dpaperband.input=card.md`
   (shows resolved id, cascade, CSS chain, block boundaries).
2. Wrong grouping/order/missing cards → `mvn paperband:structure` (shows exactly what
   `build` would render, incl. resolved index terms); remember `where:` target strings are
   unvalidated and fail silently on typos.
3. Wrong appearance → view-source the emitted HTML (`<emitHtml>`): every inlined sheet has
   a `/* === theme:name path === */` marker; remember cascade order book css → theme →
   `<stylesheets>`, and `vars.page.measure` for "margins that won't go away".
4. Card too long → `mvn paperband:pages -Dpaperband.pdf=… -Dpaperband.byPages=true`.
5. Exit codes: 2 bad input/unknown renderer · 3 page-budget violation · 4 slot contract.
6. Heading before the H1, `{{ }}`-looking prose outside code spans, a fence-attribute line
   glued to the next paragraph, and renamed published `id`s are the classic authoring traps.

## Repository map (for working on Paperband itself)

Modules: `core` (model: cards, blocks, BookConfig, Publication, CardSchema, PageSpec),
`cards` (parsing/transpiling), `config` (BookWalker, ConfigLoader cascade,
PublicationLoader), `include` (fragment tag, providers/processors, containment),
`layout` (LayoutEngine, Pebble templates, bundled themes in resources),
`render-playwright` (the renderer), `maven-plugin` (all mojos, BookBuild, PDFBox
post-processing), `archetype`, and `guide` — the self-documenting book at
`guide/src/main/paperband`, built by the plugin in the same reactor (`mvn install -Pguide`).
